ActedElement.description: An element an action acted on, as the output names it.

name.description: Its accessible name (or text), cut to 60 characters.

ref.description:
Its ref, e.g. `e6` (absent if the page changed before one could
be given).

DownloadInfo.description:
A file the browser downloaded (or is downloading) into the session's
`downloads` directory.

file.description:
The file's name, as the server suggested it (made unique in the
directory).

path.description: The absolute path of the file, once it completed.

tab.description: The tab whose page started it, if known.

total_bytes.description: The size the server announced, if it did.

error.description: What went wrong and what to run next.

events.description: Page events observed while the command ran.

ErrorInfo.description:
A command failure as the user sees it: what happened, and the next
command to run.

details.description: Structured context (candidates, observed URL, CDP error code, …).

hint.description: The concrete next command to try.

notes.description:
Short labelled facts shown between the message and the hint in the
text form (`covering: div "We use cookies" [e88]`).

ErrorKind.description:
What went wrong, as a stable machine-readable name.

The name is part of the `--json` contract (`"kind":"Timeout"`) and each
kind maps to one process exit code.

oneOf.description: No element matches the locator.
The locator matches several elements where one is needed.
Another element covers the target.
The target is disabled.
The ref is from an older snapshot.
The ref's element was removed from the page.
An `expect` assertion failed.
JavaScript threw.
Navigation failed (DNS, TLS, HTTP error page, …).
Nothing in the page says where an element came from (`source`, `components`).

A dev server's hot update failed (`wait --hmr`): the page still
runs the old code.
Bad flags or arguments.
The locator does not parse.
Something did not happen in time.
No Chrome binary was found.
Chrome was found but could not be started.
Chrome exited or the connection to it dropped.

A tab's page crashed (its renderer process died); `reload` brings
it back.
The session daemon cannot be reached or started.
Chrome rejected a CDP call.

Downloading or unpacking a browser (`chrome-cdp install`) or a
release (`chrome-cdp upgrade`) failed.
A JavaScript dialog blocks the page.
A load run's threshold failed (`chrome-cdp load`, plan 23.4).

Event.description:
Something that happened in the browser while a command ran. The
envelope lists them in `events`; the command's text says what matters.

oneOf.description:
A tab opened that no command asked for: a popup (`window.open`,
`target=_blank`) or one the user opened. It is not active unless the
session follows popups (`open --follow-popups`).

active.description: Whether it became the active tab.

opener.description: The tab that opened it, if known.

url.description: Its URL when the command ended (it may still be loading).

oneOf.description:
A JavaScript dialog closed without a `chrome-cdp dialog` command:
the session's `--dialogs` policy answered it (an `alert` or
`beforeunload` by default), or a navigation dismissed it.

by.description:
`policy` (the session's `--dialogs` answered it) or `other`
(it closed without `chrome-cdp dialog`: a navigation dismissed
it, or a raw CDP call answered it).

oneOf.description: A download started, or finished, while the command ran.

The action made the tab's main frame navigate (a link, a form, a
script): where it is now, once loaded and settled.

error.description:
Chrome's error when the page could not load
(`net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`; the tab shows an error page).

loaded.description: Whether the load event fired before the time ran out.

restored.description: It came back from the back/forward cache.

status.description:
The main document's HTTP status (absent for same-document
navigations and non-HTTP pages).

url.description: The URL it is at now.

oneOf.description:
The page logged an error (`console.error`, a failed
`console.assert`) or threw one nothing caught, after the command
began.

message.description: The message's first line, e.g. `TypeError: x is undefined`.

original.description:
Where it came from in the original source, when a source map
says so (localhost pages), with the file on disk if found.

url.description: The script it came from, with its line and column (1-based).

worker.description: The worker it came from, if a worker's.

oneOf.description:
Chrome raised an issue of severity `error` (see `issues`) after
the command began: mixed content blocked, a CORS or CSP block, …

A request of the page to its own origin failed after the command
began: an HTTP status of 400 or more, or no response.

error.description: Chrome's error if it did not, e.g. `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`.

id.description:
Its id in the tab's network log (`network show <id>`), if the
log has it.

status.description: The HTTP status, if the server answered.

oneOf.description:
A logpoint (`chrome-cdp debug log`) was hit after the command
began.

file.description: The source on disk (an absolute path), when found.

line.description: The original line it is bound at (1-based).

place.description:
Its place as text shows it: the file relative to the project root
when chrome-cdp found it, else the source's URL path, with the
line it is bound at (`src/cart.ts:42`).

values.description: Each expression's value, in the order given.

oneOf.description:
A dev server's hot update reached the tab: while an action ran,
or (on any command on the tab) since the tab's previous command.
Each is reported once.

client.description:
The dev server's client in the page: `vite`, `webpack`
(webpack-dev-server) or `next` (Next.js).

files.description:
`applied`: the files updated; `full_reload`: the file that asked
for it. Left out when the dev server does not say.

message.description: `failed`: the error's first line, as the dev server gave it.

place.description:
`failed`: where, when the error says (`source` as the dev server
names it).

oneOf.description:
Focus moved to an element of another form than before (or into a
form, or out of one, or into another frame) that the action did not
act on: a dialog or the next step of a flow took it.

frame.description:
The frame it is in, when that is not the tab's main frame: the
frame's id (what `--frame` takes; `frames` lists them).

FindingCookie.description: A cookie a finding is about.

FindingTarget.description:
What a finding is about. Every field is optional: a finding names
what it knows.

frame.description:
The frame it is in, when that is not the tab's main frame (what
`--frame` takes; `frames` lists them).

locator.description: The element's stable locator, for scripts.

ref.description: The element's ref, e.g. `e12`, while its document lives.

request_id.description: The request's id in the tab's network log (`network show <id>`).

source.description: The script and line (1-based) it comes from.

url.description:
The URL it is about: a request's, a blocked resource's, a
document's.

worker.description: The worker it came from, if a worker's.

HotFile.description: A file a hot update names.

file.description:
The file on disk (an absolute path), when chrome-cdp found it
under the project root. Text output shows it relative to the root.

source.description:
As the dev server names it: `/src/cart.ts` (Vite),
`./src/cart.ts` (webpack).

oneOf.description: The page runs the new code.

The dev server could not build it (a syntax error), or the page
could not run it: the page still runs the old code.
The dev server reloaded the page.

Issue.description:
One of Chrome's own findings about a page (`Audits.issueAdded`, the
DevTools Issues panel), in the shape every page finding has (plan
17): same `rule` and `key`, same finding.

category.description: Always `issues`: the audit category it belongs to.

count.description:
How many times Chrome raised it (occurrences with the same rule
and key are one issue).

key.description:
Its identity across runs, ports and reloads:
`issues/<rule>/<where>`, where is the element's stable locator
(else its role and name), the URL without query (`self/…` on the
page's own origin), the cookie's name and domain, or the page's
path. No refs, request ids or ports.

message.description: What is wrong, in one line.

rule.description:
A stable id: the kebab-case of Chrome's code and of its reason,
e.g. `mixed-content-blocked`,
`cookie-exclude-same-site-unspecified-treated-as-lax`;
`unknown-<code>` for a code this chrome-cdp does not know.

seq.description:
Its place in the tab's issues; later ones are larger
(`--since <seq>`).

time_ms.description:
When the daemon received it (its last occurrence), in ms since the
Unix epoch.

LoadChange.description: One number of two load runs.

marked.description: It changed by more than 10% (or from 0 to more).

LoadCompare.description:
`load --compare`: an earlier run's numbers next to this one's (plan
23.4).

changes.description:
Every number both runs have: each group's p50, p95 and p99
(p75 for a Web Vital) and the requests' error rate and rate.

marked.description: How many of them changed by more than 10%.

run.description: The earlier run's id, and its `summary.json`.

arrivals.description:
An open model's arrivals, and those dropped because `max_users`
users were running (never queued).

browser.description:
Which browser the Chromes were: `chrome-headless-shell` or
`chrome` (`--browser`).

browser_crashes.description: How many times a Chrome crashed and was started again.

browsers_started.description:
How many of them were started (with `--plan`: start before the
users; an open model's others start when first needed).

cache.description:
`[load] cache`: `new` (a fresh browser context each iteration) or
`returning` (a context per user, kept).

compare.description: `--compare`: an earlier run's numbers next to this one's.

context_setup_ms.description: The mean time making one took, in ms.

contexts.description: The browser contexts made for the users.

duration_ms.description:
How long the run took, from its first user's start to its last
iteration's end.

endpoints.description:
The requests by endpoint (`GET /api/products/:id`, `static js`),
the busiest first.

exceptions.description:
The pages' uncaught exceptions, by message, the most common first
(20 messages at most), and how many there were in all.

failures_kept.description:
The failed iterations whose page, console and requests were kept
(`--keep-failures`), and where.

iteration_ms.description:
How long an iteration took, from when it was due to start (an open
model's arrival) to its end.

journeys.description: The tests the users ran: by weight, or in turn without a profile.

max_users.description: An open model's most users at once (`max_users`).

metrics_listen.description:
`--metrics-listen`: where the live numbers were served, in
Prometheus' text format, while the run lasted.

model.description:
`open` (`[arrivals]`: users arrive at a rate) or `closed`
(`[users]`, and a run without a profile: users loop).

planned.description: `--plan`: what the run would do; nothing ran.

profile.description:
The load profile (`e2e/load/shop.toml`); absent for a run without
one.

raw.description: `--raw`: every step's start, end and result.

request_errors.description:
Failed requests by class: `http_4xx`, `http_5xx` and
`request_failed` (no response).

requests.description:
Every request the users' pages made (plan 23.4); absent when none
was.

run.description: The run's id: its folder's name.

step_times.description:
Each step's times, by its line (`step e2e/shop.cdp:14`), the
command as its label.

stopped.description: Why the run ended early, if it did.

thresholds.description:
The profile's thresholds, each checked over the whole run (with
`--plan`: as written, not checked).

users.description:
How many users ran at once, at most (with `--plan`: the users it
is expected to reach).

users_per_browser.description: The most users in one Chrome.

vitals.description:
What users saw, per page view: `ttfb`, `fcp`, `lcp`, `load` (the
load event's end), `cls` (a score) and `inp`.

LoadException.description: An uncaught exception of a load run's pages.

message.description: Its first line: `TypeError: x is undefined`.

html.description: The report as one page with charts, which opens offline.

metrics.description: One line per second per group.

LoadJourney.description: A journey of a load run.

data.description: The data file its iterations take rows from.

iteration_ms.description: How long its iterations took, from when they were due.

previous_ms.description:
With `--plan`: how long one took in an earlier run, from start to
end, if one ran.

weight.description: Its weight in the profile (1 without one).

LoadMetric.description:
One group's numbers in a load run (plan 23.4): an endpoint's requests,
a step, a journey's iterations, or a Web Vital of the page views.

cached.description: Requests a cache answered: counted, but not in the times.

error_kinds.description:
The errors by kind: a status (`500`), Chrome's error
(`net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`), a step's error kind.

errors.description:
Requests that failed or got a status of 400 or more; steps and
iterations that failed.

label.description: A step's command; a journey's test name.

phases.description: An endpoint's mean time in each phase of its requests.

rate.description: How many a second, over the run.

LoadPhases.description: The mean phases of an endpoint's requests, in ms.

connect_ms.description: Opening the connection, TLS left out.

ttfb_ms.description: Waiting for the first byte of the response: the server's time.

LoadStage.description:
A stage of a load run's model: users arriving a second (`arrivals`)
or users at once (`users`), from `from` to `to` over its duration.

LoadSteps.description: A load run's steps by result.

error.description: Any other error (no such element, a crashed browser, …).

failed.description: A check that did not hold (`expect`, `http --expect-status`).

LoadStopped.description: Why a load run ended early.

cut_short.description:
Iterations that were running and were cut short (a second Ctrl-C,
or `[load] grace` over); they are not counted.

reason.description:
`interrupted` (Ctrl-C or SIGTERM), `max_failures` (`on_failure =
"stop-run"`), `data_exhausted` (`data_exhausted = "stop"`) or
`web_server` (the backend's web server exited).

LoadThreshold.description: A threshold of a load profile (plan 23.4).

abort.description: `abort = true`: the run stops when it fails for 30 seconds in a row.

name.description: The statistic of a group, as written: `p95(GET /api/products/:id)`.

note.description: Why it has no value, and the closest groups that have one.

unit.description: `ms`, `%`, `/s`, or empty for a count or a score.

value.description:
What was measured, in `unit`; absent when nothing was (no request
had the endpoint, no page view had an INP).

LoadTimes.description: Durations of a load run, in ms.

LogpointValue.description: An expression of a logpoint, and its value at a hit.

error.description: What it threw (`ReferenceError: total is not defined`).

value.description:
Its value, previewed in the page: at most 2 levels deep, strings
cut at 80 characters, collections over 5 entries counted
(`[12 items]`), functions as `ƒ`. Absent if it threw.

Note.description: One labelled line of an error's text form.

text.description:
One line of text, or several for a block such as a diff (the
text form prints them indented under the label).

events.description:
Page events observed while the command ran (tabs opened, dialogs,
navigations, …).

truncated.description:
Values in `data` shortened to keep the output bounded; `--max-chars`
(or the command's own flag, named in the warning) shows more.

Severity.description:
How severe a finding is, most severe first (plan 17): `error` breaks
something for some users or leaks data, `warning` will break or
degrade, `info` is worth knowing. `--min-severity warning` shows
`error` and `warning`.

SourceLine.description: A place in a script: its URL, line and column (1-based).

SourcePosition.description: A place in an original source file, from a source map.

file.description:
The source on disk (an absolute path), when chrome-cdp found it:
`source` as a path, or its path's longest end that is a file under
the project root (the directory of `chrome-cdp.toml`, `.git`, …,
or `source_root` in the config). Text output shows it relative to
the root.

name.description: The original name at that place, if the map has one.

source.description:
The source file as the map names it, resolved against the map's
URL (`http://localhost:5173/src/app.ts`) unless it has its own
scheme (`webpack://app/./src/app.ts`).

TruncatedKind.description: What kind of value was shortened.

oneOf.description: Lengths count characters.
Lengths count items.

Truncation.description: One value that `--json` output shortened to fit the budget.

kept.description: How much was kept (a cut string also ends in `…`).

kind.description: A string (lengths in characters) or an array (lengths in items).

path.description: Where, as a JSON Pointer into `data` (`/result/value`).

Worker.description: A worker, as an entry of a tab's log names it.

oneOf.description: A page's or iframe's own `Worker`, of one tab.
A `SharedWorker`: of every tab of its origin.
A service worker: of every tab of its origin.
